elements.title: USING META-CHARACTERS IN REGULAR EXPRESSIONS
elements.details:
Three bullet points explaining meta-characters in regex:
- '*' matches zero or more occurrences of the preceding character or group. Example: 'a*' matches 'a', 'aa', 'aaa', etc.
- '?' matches zero or one occurrence of the preceding character or group. Example: 'a?b' matches 'ab' or 'b'.
- '+' matches one or more occurrences of the preceding character or group. Example: 'a+b' matches 'ab', 'aab', 'aaab', etc., but fails if no 'a's are present.
elements.summary: This diagram explains the use of three common meta-characters (*, ?, +) in regular expressions, illustrating their matching behavior with examples.
